test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: An item was sold for ₹40 with a profit of 15%. If it were sold for ₹36, then what would have been the percentage of profit or loss? (rounded off to 1 decimal places).
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price when profit is 15% = ₹40

Selling price if sold = ₹36

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) / (1 + Profit%)

Profit or Loss% = ((Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Cost Price when SP = ₹40 and Profit = 15%

CP = 40 / (1 + 15/100)

⇒ CP = 40 / (1.15)

⇒ CP = ₹34.78

Now, when SP = ₹36

Profit or Loss = SP - CP

⇒ Profit or Loss = 36 - 34.78

⇒ Profit = ₹1.22

Profit% = (Profit / CP) × 100

⇒ Profit% = (1.22 / 34.78) × 100

⇒ Profit% = 3.5%

**The percentage of profit is 3.5%.**
